explanation: For the perfect tree, link each left child to its sibling and each right child to the next parent’s left child. The already completed parent-level Next chain allows walking a level without a queue.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract; EPI problem attribution remains in the collection.
correctness: Before processing a level, its Next links already form the correct left-to-right chain, starting with the root’s null Next. In a perfect tree, each left child’s next neighbor is its sibling, and each right child’s next neighbor is the following parent’s left child or null. Applying these assignments across the parent chain constructs the entire next-level chain. Induction establishes every level without extra queue storage.
walkthrough: For perfect tree [16, 7, 25, 2, 11, 20, 30], set root Next to null. Link 7 → 25 → null. On the leaf level, sibling links give 2 → 11 and 20 → 30, while the cross-parent link gives 11 → 20. The complete chain is 2 → 11 → 20 → 30 → null. The adapter returns the verified levels [[16], [7, 25], [2, 11, 20, 30]].
edgeCases: Null and one-node trees need no child links.
The final node of every level must point to null.
The constant-space construction relies on the specified perfect-tree precondition.
